entries.source_definition: Young describes a pervasive medium with currents and vortices.
entries.locator: Gravity written-body aether discussion; Aether page introduction
entries.boundaries: Do not silently identify with an established modern-physics field, claim verification, or infer author adoption of geocentrism.

entries.source_definition: Earth, Water, Air and Fire function as explanatory principles in his account.
entries.locator: Gravity concluding elemental discussion; Elements introduction
entries.boundaries: Specific proportions, medical efficacy and historical lineage require additional sources; neither modern chemical elements nor personality labels by default.

entries.source_definition: His introduction relates bodily processes and the surrounding realm.
entries.boundaries: Correspondence does not itself establish identical mechanism, scale invariance or medical causation.

entries.source_definition: Selected OCR passage treats Salt as a principle associated with powdered or granulated minerals, beyond table salt.
entries.boundaries: Source-specific paraphrase; do not replace with the unverified universal equation Salt = body.

entries.source_definition: Selected OCR passage relates Sulphur to energy in matter.
entries.boundaries: This is his symbolic/principial usage; do not infer a measurable physical mechanism or universal Sulphur = soul equation.

entries.sense: Young’s alchemical prime and multiple senses
entries.source_definition: Selected OCR passages include liquid metal, solvent principle, Roman messenger and astrological planet as distinct senses.
entries.boundaries: Specify the intended sense each time. Do not collapse deity, substance, planet and principle into one referent or offer ingestion/practice advice.

entries.source_definition: Question and remove an identification or assumption while allowing inquiry to remain open.
entries.boundaries: Author working direction, not Young terminology or a universal account of all Vedantic traditions; precise traditional claims need their own primary texts.

note: Proposed source vocabulary is retrievable as attributed source material. Only separately adopted author definitions may be retrieved as current author canon.
